newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - H.Walker says hard to match work rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - H.Walker says hard to match work rise.

text.p: Contract miner and civil engineer Henry Walker Ltd said the level of work to be completed in 1996/97 would make it difficult to match the expansion in year-end work on hand achieved in 1995/96.
Managing director Richard Ryan said in the company's annual report Henry Walker had more than doubled the value of its work on hand during 1995/96 to A$829 million.
"The level of work to be completed during 1997 will make it difficult to match the expansion in year-end work on hand achieved in 1996," he said.

"However, the recent progress made by the company in its penetration of the Australian iron ore, coal and underground mining sectors, together with opportunities emerging for contractors in Asia and South America, augers well for the company's capacity for continued growth," he said.
"The outlook for Henry Walker is positive and underpinned by the company's strong order book position," he said.
Henry Walker recorded a rise in net profit in 1995/96 to A$17.69 million from A$15.55 million in 1994/95.
It said it had contracts in place at June 30, 1996 for work valued at A$275 million over the next 12 months, equivalent to about 90 percent of the 1995/96 total contracting revenue.

The company listed in the report its 1996/97 targets for a rise in revenue by "at least ten percent", an increase in earnings before interest and tax margin, and a ten percent rise in earnings per share.
